ptBR.note: Brazil writes nós falamos in the perfeito too (Portugal: falámos with an accent). Brazil also says a gente and você more often.

tandemSoGehts: Cut the cards in the middle. Partner A takes the left half, Partner B takes the right half.
A builds question 1 from the tiles and asks it: “O que é que comeste ao pequeno-almoço?” (You make the pretérito perfeito simples.)

B hears the question and builds the answer with the perfeito simples for a finished event. Endings of -ar verbs: -ei, -aste, -ou, -ámos, -aram (falei, falaste, falou, falámos, falaram). -er verbs: -i, -este, -eu, -emos, -eram (comi, comeste, comeu). -ir verbs: -i, -iste, -iu, -imos, -iram (parti, partiste, partiu). Careful: falámos (perfeito) has an accent, falamos (presente) does not. A tile in brackets like (eu) says who is speaking: it is not written.
Then B asks question 2 and A answers. Take turns. At the end, check with the answer sheet.
Last, swap cards and do it all again, faster.
